smt-2024-general-01.title: Base times height
smt-2024-general-01.body:
Take the right triangle with vertices $(0,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,1,0)$ as the base: area $\frac12$. The apex $(0,0,1)$ is at height $1$. Volume $=\frac13\cdot\frac12\cdot1=\frac16$.

**Answer: $\frac16$**

smt-2024-general-03.title: Choose the digits
smt-2024-general-03.body:
A strictly decreasing number is determined by the set of its $5$ distinct digits (which can only be written in decreasing order, and the leading digit is nonzero automatically). So the count is $\binom{10}{5}=252$.

**Answer: 252**

smt-2024-general-04.title: Go through the smallest prime
smt-2024-general-04.body:
$p=2$: need divisibility by $12$ (and even): $12,24,36,48,60,72,84,96$ -- $8$ numbers. $p=3$: need multiples of $13$ that are odd multiples of $3$ with smallest prime $3$: only $39$. $p=5$: need a multiple of $15$, but then the smallest prime would be $3$ -- none. $p\ge7$: $p(p+10)>100$ -- none. Total $8+1=9$.

**Answer: 9**

smt-2024-general-05.title: Inradius
smt-2024-general-05.body:
The region is the triangle with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(1,1)$: a right isosceles triangle with legs $\sqrt2$ and hypotenuse $2$. The largest circle inside a triangle is its incircle, with radius $r=\frac{\text{legs sum}-\text{hypotenuse}}{2}=\frac{2\sqrt2-2}{2}=\sqrt2-1$. (Also $r=\frac{\text{Area}}{s}=\frac{1}{1+\sqrt2}=\sqrt2-1$.)

**Answer: $\sqrt2-1$**

smt-2024-general-06.title: Casework on signs
smt-2024-general-06.body:
Since $|x+y|+|x-y|=2\max(|x|,|y|)$, the equation is $\max(|x|,|y|)=8$, the boundary of the square with side $16$. (Equivalently the four sign cases give $2x=16,\ 2y=16,\ -2x=16,\ -2y=16$.) Area $=16^2=256$.

**Answer: 256**

smt-2024-general-07.title: Stars and bars
smt-2024-general-07.body:
Subtract $1$ from each die: we need non-negative $y_i\le5$ with sum $5$. Since $5<6$ the upper bound is automatic, so there are $\binom{5+3}{3}=56$ outcomes out of $6^4=1296$. Probability $\frac{56}{1296}=\frac{7}{162}$.

**Answer: $\frac7{162}$**

smt-2024-general-08.title: Discriminant zero
smt-2024-general-08.body:
A double root means $r^2-4s=0$, so $s=\frac{r^2}{4}$ and $t=-\frac r2$. By Vieta on the first quadratic, $rs=-2024$, so $\frac{r^3}{4}=-2024$ and $r^3=-8096=-8\cdot1012$, i.e. $r=-2\sqrt[3]{1012}$ (the real root, as $c=-(r+s)$ must be real). Then $t=-\frac r2=\sqrt[3]{1012}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt[3]{1012}$**

smt-2024-general-10.title: Sum of products
smt-2024-general-10.body:
Roots $a,b$ with $a+b=40$ and $c=ab$. The possible $c$ are $a(40-a)$ for $a=1,\dots,20$ (distinct values). Their sum is $\sum_{a=1}^{20}(40a-a^2)=40\cdot210-2870=8400-2870=5530$.

**Answer: 5530**

smt-2024-general-11.title: Circumradius
smt-2024-general-11.body:
The center $O$ of the triangle is at distance $\frac{6}{\sqrt3}=2\sqrt3$ from each vertex. A circle about $O$ inside the circle of radius $6$ about $A$ and tangent to it has radius $6-OA=6-2\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $6-2\sqrt3$**

smt-2024-general-12.title: Chinese remainder theorem
smt-2024-general-12.body:
Modulo $8$: $x^2\equiv0$, so $4\mid x$. Modulo $125$: $x^2\equiv24\equiv1024$, so $(x-32)(x+32)\equiv0$. The two factors differ by $64$, which is not divisible by $5$, so $5$ cannot divide both: $125\mid x-32$ or $125\mid x+32$, i.e. $x\equiv\pm32\pmod{125}$. Combined with $4\mid x$: the largest $x<1000$ is $1000-32=968$ (check: $968^2=937024$).

**Answer: 968**

smt-2024-general-13.title: Casework
smt-2024-general-13.body:
A string between adjacent points (A-B, B-C, C-D, D-E) or the long string A-E never crosses another string, so each of these $5$ can be present or absent independently: $2^5=32$ choices. The other $5$ possible strings are A-C, B-D, C-E, A-D, B-E. The crossing pairs among them are A-C/B-D, B-D/C-E, C-E/A-D, A-D/B-E, B-E/A-C, which form a $5$-cycle, so we need an independent set of a $5$-cycle: $1+5+5=11$ choices (none, one string, or two non-adjacent strings). Total $32\cdot11=352$.

**Answer: 352**

smt-2024-general-13.title: Computer check
smt-2024-general-13.body:
Enumerating all subsets of the $10$ possible strings and discarding those with crossing pairs gives $352$.

**Answer: 352**

smt-2024-general-14.title: Diophantine equation
smt-2024-general-14.body:
$0.\overline4_a=\frac4{a-1}$ and $0.\overline7_b=\frac7{b-1}$, so $\frac4{a-1}+\frac7{b-1}=1$, which rearranges to $(a-5)(b-8)=28$. With $a'=a-5$, $b'=b-8$ and $a'b'=28$ we minimize $a'+b'$ (and $a+b=a'+b'+13$): the closest factor pair is $(4,7)$ or $(7,4)$, giving $a'+b'=11$ and $a+b=24$, e.g. $a=9$, $b=15$ ($a\ne b$ holds).

**Answer: 24**

smt-2024-general-15.title: Use the symmetry through the middle dodecagon
smt-2024-general-15.body:
A regular dodecagon of side $1$ has circumradius $R=\frac1{2\sin15^\circ}$ and apothem $\frac{2+\sqrt3}{2}$. In the figure the two intersection points of adjacent dodecagons are vertices of both, lying at $45^\circ$ from the line of centers, so the centers are $2R\cos45^\circ=1+\sqrt3$ apart. The picture is symmetric under a half-turn about the center $M$ of the middle dodecagon, which swaps $A$ and $B$; so $M$ is the midpoint of $AB$. Put the left center at the origin: $A=\left(-\frac12,-\frac{2+\sqrt3}{2}\right)$ and $M=(1+\sqrt3,0)$. Then $AM^2=\left(\frac32+\sqrt3\right)^2+\left(\frac{2+\sqrt3}{2}\right)^2=7+4\sqrt3=(2+\sqrt3)^2$, so $AB=2AM=4+2\sqrt3$.

**Answer: $4+2\sqrt3$**

smt-2024-general-16.title: Geometric series
smt-2024-general-16.body:
$x=1$ is never a root (all terms positive). For $x\ne1$ the equation is $\frac{x^{n+1}-1}{x-1}=0$, i.e. $x^{n+1}=1$ with $x\ne1$. The only real solution is $x=-1$, which exists exactly when $n+1$ is even, i.e. $n$ odd. So $P(n)=1$ for odd $n$ and $0$ for even $n$; the sum over $n\le2024$ is $1012$.

**Answer: 1012**

smt-2024-general-17.title: Expected change is zero
smt-2024-general-17.body:
From height $h$, one scoop gives expected height $\frac56(h+1)+\frac16\cdot\frac23h=\frac{17}{18}h+\frac56$. This equals $h$ exactly when $\frac{h}{18}=\frac56$, i.e. $h=15$; then the expectation stays $15$ after every scoop.

**Answer: 15**

smt-2024-general-18.title: Compress to a circle
smt-2024-general-18.body:
Let $M$ be the midpoint of $AB$. Since $\angle AOB=120^\circ$, $A=(-k,\,k/\sqrt3)$ for some $k>0$ (triangle $AOM$ is $30$-$60$-$90$). Substituting into the ellipse: $\frac{k^2}9+\frac{k^2}3=1$, so $k=\frac32$ and the line is $y=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$. Scaling the $x$-coordinate by $\frac13$ turns the ellipse into the unit circle and the line into $y=\frac{\sqrt3}2$, which cuts off a circular segment with central angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$: area $\frac\pi6-\frac{\sqrt3}{4}$. Scaling back multiplies areas by $3$: $\frac\pi2-\frac{3\sqrt3}{4}$.

**Answer: $\frac\pi2-\frac{3\sqrt3}4$**

smt-2024-general-19.title: Greedy: make the terms as small as possible
smt-2024-general-19.body:
To make $i$ as large as possible, each term should be as small as allowed: $a_{3k-2}$ is the smallest multiple of $8$ above $a_{3k-3}$, $a_{3k-1}=a_{3k-2}+1$, and $a_{3k}$ is the smallest multiple of $9$ above that. Between consecutive multiples of $72$ this process uses $21$ terms (each block of three terms advances by $9$ or $18$ to a multiple of $9$, and every multiple of $72$ is hit again after $7$ blocks plus the alignment). Since $\lfloor2024/72\rfloor=28$, we reach $2016=28\cdot72$ after $28\cdot21=588$ terms. Then the next term is the smallest multiple of $8$ above $2016$, which is $2024$ (term $589$, still $\le2024$), and the next is $2025$ (term $590$, $>2024$). So $i=590$ (confirmed by direct simulation).

**Answer: 590**

smt-2024-general-20.title: Linearity of expectation
smt-2024-general-20.body:
There are $8$ lines (3 rows, 3 columns, 2 diagonals). For a fixed line, consider the colors of its three cells: the probability they are all one color is $3\cdot\frac{\binom33}{\binom93}=\frac{3}{84}=\frac1{28}$ (the three cells of a color form a particular set of $3$ cells out of $\binom93=84$ equally likely sets). Expected number: $8\cdot\frac{1}{28}=\frac27$.

**Answer: $\frac27$**

smt-2024-general-21.title: Divisors of $2024^2-1$
smt-2024-general-21.body:
The conditions say exactly $n\mid2024^2-1$ and $n\nmid2024-1$. We have $2024^2-1=2023\cdot2025=(7\cdot17^2)(3^4\cdot5^2)$, which has $(2\cdot3)\cdot(5\cdot3)=90$ divisors. Divisors of $2023=2024-1$ number $2\cdot3=6$, and each divides $2024^2-1$. So the answer is $90-6=84$.

**Answer: 84**

smt-2024-general-22.title: Reciprocal roots
smt-2024-general-22.body:
The roots of $Q$ are the reciprocals of the roots of $P$ ($x\mapsto 1/x$ swaps the coefficient order), so $r_3,r_4=\frac1{r_1},\frac1{r_2}$. The sum is $S=\left(r_1+\frac4{r_1}\right)+\left(r_2+\frac4{r_2}\right)$. For positive $r$, $r+\frac4r\ge4$ with equality only at $r=2$, so $S\ge8$ with equality only if $r_1=r_2=2$, which is excluded by distinctness. Hence $S>8$, and $S=9$ is attainable (e.g. $r_1=1$, $r_2=2$ gives $1+4+2+2=9$). The smallest integer value is $9$.

**Answer: 9**

smt-2024-general-23.title: Angle chase
smt-2024-general-23.body:
Each interior angle of the pentagon is $108^\circ$. Triangle $BCF$ is equilateral, so $\angle ABF=108^\circ-60^\circ=48^\circ$; as $BA=BF=1$, $\angle AFB=\frac{180^\circ-48^\circ}2=66^\circ$. Triangle $CDG$ is equilateral, so $G$ lies on the perpendicular bisector of $CD$, which is the symmetry axis of the pentagon through $A$; hence $AG$ bisects $\angle BAE$ and $\angle BAG=54^\circ$. In triangle $CBG$, $CB=CG=1$ and $\angle BCG=108^\circ-60^\circ=48^\circ$, so $\angle CBG=66^\circ$ and $\angle GBA=108^\circ-66^\circ=42^\circ$. Then $\angle AGB=180^\circ-54^\circ-42^\circ=84^\circ$. The ratio is $\frac{66}{84}=\frac{11}{14}$.

**Answer: $\frac{11}{14}$**

smt-2024-general-25.title: Euler's theorem
smt-2024-general-25.body:
$2024=8\cdot11\cdot23=2^3\cdot253$. Every number listed is divisible by $2^3$ (exponent $\ge4$ so $4^e$ is divisible by $64$), so the remainder mod $8$ is $0$. Mod $253$: $\varphi(253)=220$, so $4^e\equiv4^{e\bmod220}$. The repdigit exponent $44\ldots4$ is $\equiv4\pmod{220}$ when it has an odd number of digits and $\equiv44\pmod{220}$ when even (because $444\equiv4$, so the residues alternate $4,44,4,44,\dots$). Then $4^4=256\equiv3\pmod{253}$ and $4^{44}\equiv3^{11}\equiv 47\pmod{253}$. Combining with $\equiv0\pmod 8$ gives remainders $x_1\equiv256$ and $x_2\equiv1312\pmod{2024}$, the only two distinct remainders. Their sum is $256+1312=1568$. (A direct computation confirms this.)

**Answer: 1568**
